answer: An operator running 184 keys therefore pays for 184 live submissions inside the window instead of preparing them in bulk, which removes the advantage of scale. Because the relic salt is published after the gale checkpoint, the nectar audit recomputes each digest and a prepared batch fails verification. Answers are salted with a 149 bit value revealed only at epoch close, so a text prepared before the reveal cannot be pre-hashed against it. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
